steps.say: Three body layers growing in the wrong postcode make a teratoma, favouring midline sites. Girls dominate, newborns grow them outside glands and teenagers inside.
steps.tx: Three germ layers in the wrong postcode make a teratoma. **Teratomas** (mixed germ tumours) mix endoderm, mesoderm and ectoderm **germ layers** (body layers) foreign to their site, favour sacrococcygeal, mediastinal, retroperitoneal and gonadal midline sites, run solid cystic or mixed and mature or immature, and affect females in **80 percent** (eighty percent) with extragonadal disease in neonates and gonadal disease in adolescents. A **mature teratoma** (ripe mixed tumour) behaves gently.

vis.alt: Gross cut specimen of a teratoma showing mixed solid and cystic tissues.
vis.caption: Cut germ cell tumour with mixed solid and cystic tissues from all germ layers. Testicular site shown; sacrococcygeal and ovarian sites share the recipe. Credit: Armed Forces Institute of Pathology.

steps.say: The tailbone tumour dominates fetal danger, robbing blood until the whole baby swells. Marker blood tests betray hidden yolk sac or placenta like elements.
steps.tx: The tailbone tumour dominates fetal danger. **Sacrococcygeal teratoma** (tailbone tumour) takes **60 percent** (sixty percent) of teratomas, large fetal masses cause polyhydramnios and **hydrops** (whole body swelling) with **vascular steal** (tumour robbing blood) high output failure and demise, and raised alpha fetoprotein or beta hCG betrays yolk sac or choriocarcinoma elements. A huge vascular tail mass threatens two lives at once.

steps.say: Cut early from behind and always take the tailbone, because the nest hides there. Leaving it multiplies return many fold.
steps.tx: Cut early, cut behind, always take the tailbone. Prompt resection prevents rupture and bleeding, the **posterior approach** (back route) with chevron cut resects tumour with **coccygectomy** (coccyx removal) preserving the anorectum, combined abdominoperineal routes handle intraabdominal extension, and missed coccyx raises **recurrence** (returning tumour) to **37 percent** (thirty seven percent) against a **4 to 11 percent** (four to eleven percent) baseline. The coccyx harbours the nest.

steps.say: Timing and markers set the outlook, with very early or late discovery warning of trouble. Track the blood marker every few months for years after surgery.
steps.tx: Timing and markers set the outlook. Diagnosis under **30 weeks** (thirty weeks) gestation or after **2 months** (two months) postnatal predicts poor **prognosis** (expected future), embryonal histology carries **15 to 20 percent** (fifteen to twenty percent) **malignant transformation** (cancer change), and alpha fetoprotein is tracked in **AFP surveillance** (marker watch) every **3 months** (three months) for **3 to 4 years** (three to four years). Rising markers after surgery mean hunt the return.

steps.say: Half of childhood ovary lumps are true tumours but few are cancers, with egg cell cancers leading. Three families divide them.
steps.tx: Half of childhood ovarian lumps are true tumours, few are cancers. Half (**50 percent**) of paediatric ovarian lesions are neoplastic as **ovarian neoplasm** (true ovary tumour) but rarely malignant, malignant lesions are **10 percent** (ten percent) of masses yet **1 percent** (one percent) of childhood cancers, and **germ cell tumour** (egg cell cancers), epithelial and **sex cord stromal tumour** (support cell tumours) families divide them. Germ cells lead in children.

steps.say: Red flags sort cancer from cyst, and a twisted ovary with a mass means theatre now. Early puberty with an ovary lump points at a hormone making tumour.
steps.tx: Red flags sort cancer from cyst. Malignancy flags are ascites, omental and peritoneal or diaphragmatic implants, adherence, aortoiliac nodes, size above **8 cm** (eight centimetres) and contralateral mass, with teratoma commonest and **ovarian torsion** (twisted ovary) complicating a quarter (**25 percent**), **dysgerminoma** (germ cell cancer) bilateral in **10 to 15 percent** (ten to fifteen percent), and granulosa tumours driving **precocious puberty** (early puberty). Torsion pain with a mass means theatre now.

steps.say: Save ovaries when benign and stage completely when not, removing cancer whole without spilling. Staging samples nodes and washings, and triple drugs cure most spread disease.
steps.tx: Save ovaries when benign, stage completely when not. Surgery means **ovarian sparing surgery** (ovary saving) for simple cysts and benign teratoma but removes tube and ovary intact for cancer without spill, with **surgical staging** (spread hunt) sampling nodes, washings, implants and contralateral ovary by sight, with **BEP chemotherapy** (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) for spread disease curing **87.5 percent** (eighty seven point five percent) event free and **93.8 percent** (ninety three point eight percent) overall in stage II.

vis.alt: FIGO staging diagrams of ovarian cancer spread from stage one to four.
vis.caption: Adult FIGO staging of ovarian spread. Paediatric germ cell surgery follows the same spread logic with marker staging. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Surface tumours are rare guests in children, while hormone making tumours announce themselves. Unwanted hair and deepening voice with an ovary mass point straight at the rare one.
steps.tx: Surface tumours are rare guests in children. **Epithelial tumours** (surface cancers) stay under **20 percent** (twenty percent) of paediatric ovarian masses as serous or mucinous **cystadenoma** (cystic adenoma) to carcinoma, and androgenic **Sertoli Leydig tumour** (testosterone tumour) raises testosterone metabolites. Virilisation with an ovary mass points straight at this rare tumour.
